Flight Control v1.4.0 (Apache-2.0, Red Hat-led): an agent on each device 'always calls home' to the service (devices may sit on private networks), enrolls with a fleet-wide enrollment certificate, generates an optional TPM-bound key pair, submits a CSR, and an EnrollmentRequest waits until an operator runs 'flightctl approve' (optionally adding labels); afterwards all agent traffic is mTLS; lifecycle states Factory -> Enrolled -> Managed -> Decommissioned

Flight Control v1.4.0 fleets: rollouts use a BatchSequence strategy; batches update in order and the next batch starts only if the previous batch's success ratio meets the configured success threshold; the final batch is implicit (all remaining devices); the agent stages assets first and rolls back the OS image and configuration if the update fails or greenboot health checks fail after reboot

AWS IoT Greengrass v2 docs: a core device runs the Greengrass Core software (nucleus in Java, or since 2.14 the smaller C 'nucleus lite') on Linux or Windows, ARM or x86, and is an AWS IoT thing grouped in thing groups; client devices (FreeRTOS or Device SDK) connect to a core device over MQTT and the core relays between them, components and AWS IoT Core; deployments to a device or thing group are 'continuous'; downloading the Core software means agreeing to the Greengrass Core Software License Agreement although the nucleus repository on GitHub is Apache-2.0

Siemens Industrial Edge architecture page: Industrial Edge Management (IEM) comes as IEM Virtual (on-prem virtual appliance), IEM Pro (on Kubernetes) and IEM Cloud (Siemens-hosted), plus an air-gapped IEM; Edge Runtime runs on SIMATIC IPCs, IoT/SCALANCE devices, HMI panels, certified third-party hardware or as a virtual edge device; apps are 'Docker-standard containers'; zero-touch provisioning and remote configuration are claimed; offline device behaviour is not described

Siemens Industrial Edge licensing (product page, via search result): each onboarded Industrial Edge device requires one Industrial Edge Management license; one is included with each Industrial Edge Hub access

Azure IoT Operations overview (updated 2026-11-11): data services on Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes at the edge (edge MQTT broker, Akri connectors, data flows), managed from the cloud through Azure Arc; assets are stored in Azure Device Registry in the cloud; it 'Can operate offline for a maximum of 72 hours. Degradation might occur during this period'; Essentials SKU (from 1.5.x) is single-node only and lacks the OPC UA connector

Litmus Edge docs: 'an Industrial Edge Data Platform that allows you to collect, analyze, and act on real-time data at the edge', with native drivers for industrial devices, control systems and robotics, container-based applications on top of the data, and 'offline-first and air-gapped installation'; the overview page does not describe central management or licensing

Anduril Lattice developer docs (public): the 'Lattice SDK allows developers to build applications, data services, and hardware integrations'; integration entry points include the Entities API and Tasks API; Lattice supports REST (web apps, dashboards) and gRPC ('Best for hardware integrations publishing high-frequency telemetry from drones, robots, and sensors'); the overview page says nothing about approval of tasks
The anduril/lattice-sdk-python repository LICENSE is the proprietary 'Anduril Lattice Software Development Kit (SDK) License Agreement', not an open-source licence (GitHub reports NOASSERTION)

Open-RMF README: 'The Open-RMF platform for multi-fleet robot management', a collection of packages with ROS 2 dependencies distributed for ROS 2 Humble, Jazzy, Kilted and Rolling, as Debian packages on Ubuntu and some RPMs for RHEL/Fedora, amd64 and aarch64; Apache-2.0

Home Assistant remote-access docs: Home Assistant Cloud gives remote access 'without opening any ports on your router'; alternatives are a VPN 'such as Tailscale or ZeroTier One' or router port forwarding; the page says nothing about connecting several Home Assistant instances together
